title: Desktop browser view and email sign-in link (owner requests, 2026-11-06)
steps: DESKTOP BROWSER VIEW (owner request; PRD §7, §15, §16). The app stays iPhone-first, but every screen must also be a first-class desktop browser experience, not a stretched phone layout. Read the current shell (src/routes/(app)/+layout.svelte, the bottom nav, nav.ts, the glass and safe-area styles), docs/design-system.md and the screens on main, and plan: (1) breakpoints and layout tokens added to the design system (phone < 640 px, tablet 640-1023 px, desktop >= 1024 px), documented in docs/design-system.md with the rules for content width (a readable column on forms and text, wider grids for dashboards), density, hover and focus states for pointer devices (`@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`), and keyboard use; (2) a responsive app shell: below 1024 px the existing bottom nav, unchanged; at 1024 px and up a left navigation rail or sidebar with the same five destinations, `aria-current`, a visible focus ring and the same order, the content area centred with a max width, no glass bar at the bottom, and the theme and offline states intact; CSS only where possible so no route gains initial JS (budgets: initial JS <= 60 KB gzip per route, `/profile/security` has under 1 KB headroom); (3) the screens that exist on main (sign-in, setup, recover, Today, Train, Coach, Progress, Profile, Profile → Security, the design gallery, offline) checked and adjusted at desktop widths, e.g. Profile's section list and the editor side by side; (4) a Playwright `desktop-chromium` project (and `desktop-webkit` in CI, where WebKit runs) at 1440 x 900 that runs the shell spec and the key screen specs, with screenshots of every main screen at desktop size in CI artifacts, and the mobile projects unchanged; (5) a rule for every later UI slice: it is designed and verified at both the iPhone viewport and 1440 px wide (add it where the testing and design docs state the UI rules). The M2 and M3 screen slices land in parallel: plan the shell and the rules first so they build on them, and one later pass that adjusts the screens those slices add.

EMAIL SIGN-IN LINK (owner request; PRD §13). Add 'Email me a sign-in link' to the sign-in screen as a second way in, next to passkeys (which stay primary). Decisions already made by the owner: the email service is Resend's HTTP API on its free tier (RESEND_API_KEY, Production only, Sensitive; until the owner verifies nikocruz.com in Resend the sender is Resend's onboarding address, so EMAIL_FROM is configurable); the link may ONLY ever go to the owner's address, which is configuration (OWNER_EMAIL, set to the owner's Gmail in Vercel; never committed, never taken from the request: the request carries no address at all); a link sign-in is a FULL session, but the sensitive actions that already require step-up re-authentication (adding or removing passkeys, new recovery codes, signing out other devices) still require a passkey. Plan, against the existing auth code (src/lib/server/auth/*, ADR 0006, docs/security.md, the rate limits, audit log, Origin checks and deny-by-default route table): a single-use link token of at least 256 bits from the platform CSPRNG, stored only as a SHA-256 hash, valid 15 minutes, consumed atomically (concurrent use cannot create two sessions), refused after use or expiry; requesting a link is rate-limited per IP and globally and always answers the same (it never says whether an owner exists or whether mail was sent); the emailed URL opens a page that needs one tap to sign in (POST), so mail scanners that prefetch links cannot consume or use the token; the email itself is plain and safe (no tracking, the link's expiry stated, a note that it can be ignored); audit-log events for requested, sent, used, expired and refused; the feature switches itself off (the option is hidden and the endpoint answers 404) when RESEND_API_KEY or OWNER_EMAIL is missing, so production keeps working before the owner sets them; a provider interface with the Resend adapter and a test adapter that records messages so integration and Playwright tests read the link without real email (behind the existing test-only route rules, refused on hosted deployments); an ADR (0011) and a new docs/security.md section with the threat model (a compromised mailbox, link forwarding, prefetching, replay, enumeration) and why step-up still guards sensitive changes; docs/deployment.md and docs/environment.md list the new variables. Any migration joins the strict migration chain after the migrations already on main and in M3's schema track.

DOCS AND STATUS: docs/product-requirements.md and docs/milestones.md record both requests (the docs PR for that may already exist: check open PRs); this plan's final slice brings docs/testing.md, docs/design-system.md and docs/security.md up to date in one docs pass if earlier slices did not.
acceptance: Desktop: at 1440 x 900 every main screen is laid out for the width (navigation rail, centred content, no stretched phone layout, no horizontal scroll), keyboard and pointer states work, and Playwright desktop specs and screenshots run in CI on Chromium and WebKit; the iPhone viewport is unchanged and its specs still pass; no route's initial JS grows past its budget.

Email link: Playwright (Chromium) requests a link from the sign-in screen, reads it from the test mail adapter, opens it, taps to sign in and lands on Today; a used or expired link, a second concurrent use, and a link-prefetch GET are all refused or harmless (integration tests on real Postgres); the request never takes an address and only ever mails OWNER_EMAIL (tested); rate limits apply; after a link sign-in, adding a passkey still asks for a passkey step-up; with RESEND_API_KEY or OWNER_EMAIL unset the option is hidden and the endpoint answers 404; no secret reaches the browser bundle.

Docs: ADR 0011, docs/security.md (threat model), docs/design-system.md (breakpoints and desktop rules), docs/deployment.md and docs/environment.md (RESEND_API_KEY, OWNER_EMAIL, EMAIL_FROM) are accurate.
